problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨1,\,t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-\frac{t}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}},\,\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given a General Parametrization
examples.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 2\sin t, \:2\cos t \right\rangle.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $\mathbf T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\mathbf \kappa(t) = \dfrac{\left\| \mathbf T'(t) \right\|}{\| \mathbf r'(t) \|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s,$ where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2},\,\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2}⟩,\,0<s<\frac{1}{2}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (2s)^{1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨-(1-2s)^{1/2},\,(2s)^{1/2}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-(1-2s)^{1/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}((2s)^{1/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{-1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{2}(2s)^{-1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨(1-2s)^{-1/2},\,(2s)^{-1/2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, the curvature is  

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{((1-2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}+{((2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(1-2s)^{-1}+(2s)^{-1}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-2s}+\frac{1}{2s}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2s(1-2s)}}.\end{aligned}
$$
